# State, sensors, and actuators

The I/O contract is the same in every engine: read configuration and velocity, read body/link poses, write **controls** (dynamic) or **state** (kinematic), optionally read **sensors** after the step stage that fills them. MJCF actuators and sensors: [MuJoCo XML reference](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/XMLreference.html); overview in [References — Robotics assets](references.qmd#robotics-assets).

Runnable reference (AgileX Piper Menagerie scene):

```bash
uv sync --extra sim
uv run python scripts/mujoco_robot_demo.py
uv run python scripts/motrix_robot_demo.py
```

## Read / write map

| What | MuJoCo (`MjData`) | Motrix (`SceneData`) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Joint positions | `data.qpos` | `data.dof_pos` or `joint.get_dof_pos(data)` | Shape `(nq,)` / `(num_dof,)` — **DoF** scalars, not joint-object count; see [Joint vs DoF](rotations-and-frames.qmd#joint-vs-dof) |
| Joint velocities | `data.qvel` | `data.dof_vel` or `joint.get_dof_vel(data)` | Same |
| Actuator controls | `data.ctrl` | `data.actuator_ctrls` or `actuator.set_ctrl(data, v)` | **Dynamic** input to `step` |
| Body pose (world) | `data.xpos[i]`, `data.xquat[i]` | `link.get_pose(data)` | After FK or `step` |
| Reset | `mj_resetData` / manual zero | `data.reset(model)` | Returns to keyframe / default |

Menagerie Piper **position actuators** (`<position …/>` in MJCF): `ctrl` is a **target joint position**, not motor torque. The internal PD drives `qpos` toward `ctrl` during `step`.

Menagerie Piper **motor actuators** (`<motor …/>`): `ctrl` is a **joint torque** (Nm). There is no built-in servo — you implement PD (or any controller) in Python and write `tau` each tick.

| Actuator | `ctrl` meaning | Who closes the loop |
|---|---|---|
| `<position>` | Target joint angle `q*` | **Simulator** — stiffness `kp`, damping `kv` in MJCF |
| `<motor>` | Joint torque `τ` | **You** — explicit PD, computed torque, RL policy, etc. |

See [Simulation stability — position vs motor](simulation-stability.qmd#position-vs-motor-actuators) for how this interacts with substeps.

## Joint PD control

To move a hinge toward a **target angle** `q*` (and optionally a **target velocity**
`q̇*`), the usual model is a **PD servo** that outputs joint torque:

$$
\tau = K_p\,(q^* - q) + K_d\,(\dot q^* - \dot q)
$$

- **`K_p`** (stiffness): pulls `q` toward `q*`. Larger ⇒ snappier tracking, but
  harder to integrate stably at large `Δt_sim`.
- **`K_d`** (damping): opposes velocity error. When **`q̇* = 0`** (the common case —
  “hold this angle”), this reduces to **`-K_d q̇`**, i.e. viscous damping that
  fights overshoot and oscillation.

**Too much stiffness or too little damping** can destabilize the integrator even
 when `Δt_sim` is modest — the inner PD behaves like a stiff spring-mass that
 explicit integrators (and large steps) cannot resolve. Symptoms match other
 instability modes: growing `qvel`, oscillation, poor tracking. Runnable examples
 at `Δt_sim = 10 ms` (Euler): **`5× kp`** or **`kv = 0`** on Piper position
 actuators fail the seed-0 reach test; nominal Menagerie gains pass
 (`scripts/pd_gain_stability_demo.py`). See also [Simulation
 stability](simulation-stability.qmd#stiff-pd-gains).

Menagerie Piper encodes these gains on **position** actuators in MJCF (`kp`, `kv`
 on `joint1`–`joint6` in `piper.xml`). You write **`q*`** into `ctrl`; MuJoCo
 applies the PD law inside every `step()` and respects actuator force limits
 (`forcerange` on the default class).

With **motor** actuators there is no built-in servo — **you** evaluate the same
 law and write **`τ`** into `ctrl`:

```python
# q_des, q, qd: vectors for the arm DoFs; Kp, Kd per joint (match MJCF kp/kv)
tau = Kp * (q_des - q) + Kd * (0.0 - qd)   # hold still → qdot_star = 0
tau = np.clip(tau, -tau_limit, tau_limit)  # respect ctrlrange / gear limits
data.ctrl[actuator_ids] = tau
```

The motor path in `scripts/actuator_control_demo.py` uses Piper’s numeric gains
 (`Kp = 80, 80, 80, 40, 10, 10` and `Kd = 5, 5, 5, 5, 1.5, 1.5` on the six arm
 joints) and recomputes `tau` **every physics substep** — holding torque at
 controller rate only fails the reach test ([Simulation
 stability](simulation-stability.qmd#position-vs-motor-actuators)).

| You command | Actuator type | Who evaluates PD |
|---|---|---|
| `q*` | `<position>` | Simulator (each `step`) |
| `τ` from PD(`q*`, `q`, `q̇*`) | `<motor>` | Your code (each `step` or substep) |

**Do not confuse** joint PD with the tiny **outer P** in the robot demos below:
 that loop nudges the **position target** `q*` itself (`ctrl ← q + α(q_goal - q)`),
 not the torque. IK + position actuators is another outer loop: it updates `q*`
 from workspace error; the inner PD still runs in the engine.

## Dynamic vs kinematic writes

- **Write controls** (`data.ctrl` / `set_ctrl`) — the **dynamic** path: actuators apply forces/torques (or position servos) inside `step`. Use for simulating motors.
- **Write state** (`qpos` / `set_dof_pos`) — the **kinematic** path: teleport the robot, then call FK (`mj_forward` / `forward_kinematic`). Use for resets, IK solutions, debugging geometry. Do not set `qpos` every step *and* expect realistic physics unless you mean to kinematically track.

See [Kinematics vs dynamics](kinematics-vs-dynamics.qmd#kinematics-vs-dynamics).

## Tiny outer P on position targets (MuJoCo)

From the lockstep section of `scripts/mujoco_robot_demo.py` — read `q`, nudge the
**position target** (not torque), step. This is a slow outer loop on `q*`; the
**inner joint PD** (previous section) still runs inside `step`:

```python
err = target_q - data.qpos[0]
data.ctrl[0] = data.qpos[0] + 0.35 * err   # outer P on actuator target
mj.mj_step(model, data)
```

Motrix equivalent:

```python
q = float(joint1.get_dof_pos(data))
act.set_ctrl(data, q + 0.35 * (target_q - q))
step(model, data)
```

In Isaac Lab the same idea is `set_joint_position_target` → `write_data_to_sim()` → `sim.step()` → `articulation.update(dt)` ([Two simulators — Isaac Lab](two-simulators.qmd#isaac-lab)).

## Sensors

Sensors are declared in MJCF (`<sensor>`). Read them **after** the pipeline stage that computes sensor values (typically after `step`, or after `mj_sensorPos` in MuJoCo if you split stages).

| | MuJoCo | Motrix |
|---|---|---|
| Raw array | `data.sensordata[adr:adr+dim]` | via `model.get_sensor_value(id, data)` |
| Named lookup | `mj_name2id` + sensor address | `model.get_sensor(…)` |

The Piper tutorial scene has no extra sensors beyond implicit state; add `<framepos>`, `<jointpos>`, IMU blocks in MJCF when you need them.

## Batched / vectorized sim

MuJoCo: one `(MjModel, MjData)` pair per instance (or `mj_data` batch in advanced use). Motrix: multiple `SceneData` from one `SceneModel`. Isaac Lab: `num_envs` articulation tensors — see [Two simulators](two-simulators.qmd#two-simulators) Isaac table.

Keep joint indices and actuator names stable — [Scene vocabulary](scene-vocabulary.qmd#scene-vocabulary) and [Asset files](asset-files.qmd#asset-files) define where they come from on disk.
